blocks.html:
Exposé X
COHOMOLOGICAL DIMENSION: FIRST RESULTSby M. Artin
Contents

1. Introduction
2. Auxiliary results for a field
3. Field of fractions of a strictly local ring
4. Cohomological dimension: the case \(\ell\) invertible in \(\mathcal{O}_X\)
5. Cohomological dimension: the case \(\ell = p\).
6. Cohomological dimension for a prescheme of finite type over Spec \(\mathbb{Z}\).
1. Introduction
In this exposé we agree, unless expressly stated otherwise, that "sheaf" means "abelian sheaf".

Let \(X\) be a scheme and \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\). We "recall" that one calls the \(\ell\)-cohomological dimension of \(X\) the largest integer \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell X = n\) (or \(= \infty\) if this number does not exist) such that \(H^n(X,F) \neq 0\) for at least one \(\ell\)-torsion sheaf \(F\) on \(X\). If \(X = \operatorname{Spec} A\), we write \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell A = \operatorname{cd}_\ell \operatorname{Spec} A\). Taking into account the dictionary (VIII 2), one thus recovers the "classical" notion of \([\mathrm{CG}]\) in the case where \(A = k\) is a field. Since we obviously have the formula \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell \left( \coprod_i X_i \right) = \sup_i \operatorname{cd}_\ell X_i \] one can, in an evident way, extend the classical theory to an arbitrary artinian ring. This theory is presented in \((\mathrm{CG}) = \) Serre's "cohomologie Galoisienne". We will add some further details in n° 2.

Take for example the case of an irreducible algebraic variety \(X\), of dimension \(n\), over a separably closed field \(k\), and fix \(\ell \neq \operatorname{car} k\). A theorem which will be found in n° 4 gives for the cohomological dimension the upper bound \(2n\), which is the "true" dimension of \(X\) (suggested by the topological analogy in the case where \(k = \mathbb{C}\)). This result is fairly elementary starting from the theory for fields, and in fact the bound \(2n\) can be improved except in the case where \(X\) is complete: there is another bound, \(2n-1\), which holds whenever \(X\) is "missing at least one point". This last bound is the correct "stable bound", in the sense that every \(X\) of dimension \(n\) contains an open subset of cohomological dimension \(2n-1\). A third bound is obtained for an affine variety, where one obtains \(n\) as the cohomological dimension. This is a generalization of one of Lefschetz's theorems on hyperplane sections. These last two assertions are deeper and can only be proved later (XIV).

Note that cohomological dimension is not a local notion (contrary to what happens in paracompact spaces). For example, a henselian ring with separably closed residue field has cohomological dimension zero, but if one removes the closed point, one can obtain an arbitrarily large number, namely \(2n-1\) if \(n = \dim A\) in the most important cases; which is also in agreement with the topological analogy provided by the cohomology of \(U - \{x\}\), where \(U\) is a small open neighbourhood of a point \(x\) of a complex analytic space.
2. Auxiliary results over a field
We have the following

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 2.1

Let \(k'/k\) be a finitely generated extension of a field \(k\), and let \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\). Then \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell k' \leqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell k + \operatorname{deg.tr.}(k'/k) , \] If the strict inequality holds and if \(\ell \neq \operatorname{car} k\), then \(\ell = 2\), \(k\) is orderable, and \(k'\) is not orderable (i.e. \(-1\) is a sum of squares in \(k'\)).

Recall that when \(\ell = \operatorname{car} k\) one has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k \leqslant 1\) (CG II 2.2), so the question of equality in 2.1 hardly arises. Moreover, one has \(\operatorname{cd}_2 k = \infty\) if \(k\) is orderable. Indeed, the algebraic closure \(\bar{k}\) of \(k\) contains a subextension \(\tilde{k}\) (a maximal ordered subfield of \(\bar{k}\)) with \([\bar{k}:\tilde{k}] = 2\). Obviously, \(\operatorname{cd}_2 \tilde{k} = \infty\), and \(\operatorname{cd}_2 \tilde{k} \leqslant \operatorname{cd}_2 k\) by (CG I Prop. 14).

Proof. This is almost all well known. The inequality, as well as the equality if \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k' < \infty\), are results of Tate (CG II 4.1.2). It remains to prove that \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k' < \infty\) and \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k = \infty\) imply \(k\) orderable and \(\ell = 2\), and it suffices to treat the two following cases:

1. a) \([k':k] < \infty\),
  2. b) \(k' = k(x)\) with \(x\) transcendental over \(k\).

In case a) one can assume \(k'/k\) separable. Then the Galois group \(H = G(\bar{k}/k')\) is an open subgroup of \(G = G(\bar{k}/k)\), and by a result of Serre [5] one has \(\operatorname{cd} H = \operatorname{cd} G\) unless \(G\) contains an element of order \(\ell\). Since an algebraically closed field \(\bar{k}\) cannot have a subfield \(\tilde{k}\) of finite index unless \(\ell = 2\) and \(\tilde{k}\) is orderable [7], we obtain the result.

Let us treat case b). Let \(R\) be the henselization of \(\operatorname{Spec} k[x]\) at the point \(x = 0\), which is a discrete valuation ring, and let \(K\) be the field of fractions of \(R\). Then \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k(x) < \infty\) implies \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell K < \infty\). It thus suffices to prove that \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell K < \infty\) implies \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k < \infty\), which is a consequence of the following theorem:

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 2.2(∗)

Let \(R\) be a henselian discrete valuation ring, with field of fractions \(K\) and residue field \(k\). Let \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\). One has \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell K = \operatorname{cd}_\ell k + 1 \] in the two following situations:

  1. (i) \(\ell \neq \operatorname{car} k\).
  2. (ii) \(\ell = \operatorname{car} K\), \(k\) perfect, and \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k < \infty\).

blocks.title: Remark
blocks.html:
Remark

Naturally, if \(\ell = \operatorname{car} K\) one has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell K \leqslant 1\) in any case (CG II 2.2). It thus remains to study the relation of \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell K\) with, perhaps, the module of absolute differentials \(\Omega^1_k\) (EGA IV 20.4.3), in the unequal-characteristic case when \(\operatorname{car} k = \ell\), \(k\) not perfect.

Proof of the theorem. As for theorem (2.1), most of it is due to Tate. Case (ii) is treated explicitly in (CG II Prop. 12) if \(R\) is complete, and one reduces to this case by means of the following lemma:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 2.2.1

Let \(R\) be a henselian discrete valuation ring, with field of fractions \(K\), and let \(\hat{K}\) be the field of fractions of the completion \(\hat{R}\) of \(R\). Then \[ G(\overline{\hat{K}}/\hat{K}) \simeq G(\overline{K}/K) . \]

Proof. This means that the functor \(L \longmapsto \hat{L} = L \otimes_K \hat{K}\) from the category of étale \(K\)-algebras to the category of étale \(\hat{K}\)-algebras is an equivalence. Now every étale algebra \(\hat{K}'\) of \(\hat{K}\) is induced by a suitable étale algebra \(K'\) of \(K\). Indeed, if \(\hat{K}' = \hat{K}[\alpha]\) where \(\alpha\) satisfies the separable irreducible equation \(f(T) = 0\) with coefficients in \(\hat{R}\), it suffices to take for \(K'\) the algebra \(K[\alpha_0]\), where \(\alpha_0\) is a root of an equation \(f_0(T) = 0\) with coefficients in \(R\) with \(f_0 \equiv f \ (\hat{\mathfrak{m}}^N)\), \(N\) large and \(\hat{\mathfrak{m}}\) the maximal ideal of \(\hat{R}\). This is the application of the usual "Newton's method" (Bourbaki, Alg. Comm. III 4.5). It remains to prove that the functor is fully faithful (it is obviously faithful), and it amounts to the same to prove that if \(K'\) is a field, so is \(\hat{K}'\). Let \(R'\) be the normalization of \(R\) in \(K'\), which is finite over \(R\) since \(K'/K\) is separable. The ring \(R'\) is a discrete valuation ring, and the completion of \(R'\) is \(\hat{R}' = R' \otimes_R \hat{R}\). Hence \(\hat{R}'\) is a discrete valuation ring, and since \(\hat{K}'\) is its total ring of fractions, it is indeed a field.

Let us treat assertion i) of 2.2. If \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k < \infty\), we are again reduced by 2.2.1 to (CG II Prop. 12) (the assumption made in the statement of this proposition that \(k\) be perfect is used in the proof only in the case of residue characteristic \(\ell\)). It thus remains to prove that \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell K < \infty\) implies \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k < \infty\).

Let \(\overline{G} = G(\bar{k}/k) = G(\widetilde{K}/K)\) where \(\widetilde{K}\) is the maximal unramified extension of \(K\) (i.e. the field of fractions of the discrete valuation ring \(\widetilde{R}\), with separably closed residue field, the strict henselization of \(R\)), \(G = G(\overline{K}/K)\), \(H = G(\overline{K}/\widetilde{K})\), so \(\overline{G} = G/H\). Let \(\overline{G}' \subset \overline{G}\) be a Sylow \(\ell\)-subgroup, and let \(k'/k\), \(K'/K\) be the extensions corresponding to \(\overline{G}'\). One has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k < \infty\) if and only if \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k' < \infty\) (CG I Prop. 14), so by replacing \(R\) by its normalization in \(K'\), one reduces to the case where \(\overline{G}\) is an \(\ell\)-group. It then suffices to prove that if \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell G < \infty\), then \(H^N(\overline{G}, \mathbb{Z}/\ell) = 0\) for \(N\) sufficiently large (CG I Prop. 20).
One has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell H = 1\) by the part of i) already proved, applied to \(\widetilde{R}\). Moreover, one has
(2.2.2) \[ H^1(H, \mu_\ell) = H^1(\operatorname{Spec} \widetilde{K}, \mu_\ell) = \widetilde{K}^*/\widetilde{K}^{*\ell} = \mathbb{Z}/\ell . \]

Indeed, \(H^1(\operatorname{Spec} \widetilde{K}, \mu_\ell) = \widetilde{K}^*/\widetilde{K}^{*\ell}\) by Kummer theory IX 3.2. One has an exact sequence \[ 0 \longrightarrow \widetilde{R}^* \longrightarrow \widetilde{K}^* \longrightarrow \mathbb{Z} \longrightarrow 0 , \] and \(\widetilde{R}^*\) is divisible by \(\ell\) since \(\widetilde{R}\) is strictly local and \(\ell\) is invertible in \(\widetilde{R}\), whence (2.2.2).
Consider the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence \[ E_2^{pq} = H^p(\overline{G}, H^q(H, \mu_\ell)) \Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(G, \mu_\ell) . \]

One has \(E_2^{pq} = 0\) if \(q > 1\). If moreover \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell G < \infty\), the "coboundary" morphism \[ H^{n-1}(\overline{G}, H^1(H, \mu_\ell)) \longrightarrow H^{n+1}(\overline{G}, \mu_\ell) \] must be bijective for \(n\) sufficiently large, and one must prove that then \[ H^{n-1}(\overline{G}, H^1(H, \mu_\ell)) = H^{n-1}(\overline{G}, \mathbb{Z}/\ell) = 0 . \]

Set \(R' = R[x']\) with \(x'^\ell = x\), \(x\) the local parameter of \(R\), and let \(K'\) be the field of fractions of \(R'\), \(G' = G(\overline{K}/K')\), etc. The residue field of \(R'\) is \(k\), since we have assumed \(\overline{G}\) to be an \(\ell\)-group, hence that the \(\ell\)-th roots of unity are in \(K\). We have a diagram \[ \xymatrix{ H' \ar[r] \ar[d] & G' \ar[r] \ar[d] & \overline{G} \ar@{=}[d] \\ H \ar[r] & G \ar[r] & \overline{G} } \] whence a morphism of Hochschild-Serre spectral sequences, which gives a commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix@R=3em{ H^{n-1}(\overline{G}, H^1(H', \mu_\ell)) \ar[dr] & \\ & H^{n+1}(\overline{G}, \mu_\ell) \\ H^{n-1}(\overline{G}, H^1(H, \mu_\ell)) \ar[uu]^{\varepsilon} \ar[ur] & } \] Since \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell G < \infty\) implies \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell G' < \infty\), all the morphisms in this diagram are isomorphisms for \(n\) large. But the morphism \[ \mathbb{Z}/\ell = H^1(H, \mu_\ell) \longrightarrow H^1(H', \mu_\ell) = \mathbb{Z}/\ell \] which induces the arrow \(\varepsilon\) is obviously zero, so \(H^{n-1}(\overline{G}, \mathbb{Z}/\ell) = 0\), q.e.d.

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 2.3

Let \(A\) be a henselian noetherian ring of dimension 1, and \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\) invertible in \(A\). Let \(k\) be the residue field of \(A\) and \(R(A)\) the ring of rational functions on \(\operatorname{Spec} A\). One has \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A) \leqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell k + 1 , \] and equality holds if \(\ell \neq 2\) or if \(k\) is not orderable.

Proof. By replacing \(A\) by \(A/P\) for a minimal prime ideal \(P\) of \(A\) and applying (VIII 1), one sees that one can assume \(A\) integral. Let \(K\) be its field of fractions, \(R\) its normalization, which is local and henselian, hence a discrete valuation ring (it is noetherian by Krull-Akizuki (Bourbaki, Alg. Comm. Chap. 7, § 2, prop. 5)), and let \(k'\) be the residue field of \(R\). It is known that \([k':k] < \infty\) (loc. cit.). Now \(K\) is the field of fractions of \(R\) and one thus has \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell K = \operatorname{cd}_\ell k' + 1 \leqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell k + 1 \] by 2.2, with equality under the last hypothesis of 2.3, by 2.1.

blocks.title: Example
blocks.html:
Example

Equality does not hold for \(\ell = 2\), \(A\) being the henselization at the origin of \(\mathbb{R}[x,y]/(x^2+y^2)\).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 2.4

Let \(A\) be a noetherian local ring with residue field \(k\), and let \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\) be invertible in \(A\). Suppose that \(\ell \neq 2\) or that no residue field of \(\operatorname{Spec} A\) is orderable. Then one has \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A) \geqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell k + \dim A , \] where \(R(A)\) is the ring of rational functions on \(\operatorname{Spec} A\).

Proof. One can assume \(A\) integral, with field of fractions \(R(A) = K\). Let \(x \in \mathfrak{r}A\) be an element which is not a zero-divisor. Then \(\dim A/(x) = \dim A - 1\). By induction on \(\dim A\), one has \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A/(x)) \geqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell k + \dim A - 1 . \] Let \(k'\) be a residue field of \(R(A/(x))\) such that \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k' = \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A/(x))\) (cf. VIII 1), and let \(P\) be the prime ideal, kernel of \(A \longrightarrow k'\). The ring \(A_P\) has dimension 1. It thus suffices to prove the corollary for the local ring \(A_P\), that is, one is reduced to the case where \(\dim A = 1\). Let \(\widetilde{A}\) be the henselization of \(A\). Each residue field of \(R(\widetilde{A})\) is identified with a separable extension of \(R(\widetilde{A}) = K\), and one thus has \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A) = \operatorname{cd}_\ell K \geqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(\widetilde{A}) . \] One is thus reduced to the case where \(A\) is of dimension 1 and henselian, which is a consequence of 2.3.

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 2.5

Let \(X\) be a noetherian scheme and let \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\) be invertible on \(X\). Then \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(X) \geqslant \dim X . \]

Indeed, let \(x \in X\) be a point such that \(\dim X = \dim \mathcal{O}_{X,x}\) (or such that \(\dim \mathcal{O}_{X,x}\) is very large if \(\dim X = \infty\)). Let \(A\) be the strict henselization of \(\mathcal{O}_{X,x}\). Then one has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell R(X) \geqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(\mathcal{O}_{X,x}) \geqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A)\) by the usual reasoning. Moreover, \(\dim A = \dim X\) (resp. is very large). If \(\ell = 2\), and if \(\ell\) is invertible on \(X\), then the equation \(T^2+ 1 = 0\) is separable over \(A\), so \(-1\) is a square in \(A\) because \(A\) is strictly local, hence the residue fields of \(A\) are non-orderable. Hence the hypotheses of 2.4 are satisfied for \(A\) in any case, and one has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A) \geqslant \dim A\), whence the result.

footnotes.html: (∗) This theorem was recently proved by Ax [1].

pages.title: 3. Field of fractions of a strictly local ring

blocks.html: 3. Field of fractions of a strictly local ring

We will have an essential need, for the sections that follow, of knowledge of \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A)\), where \(A\) is a strictly local ring, that is, henselian with separably closed residue field. Unfortunately, \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A)\) is not known in the general case, for example if \(A = \hat{\mathbb{Z}}_p[[x]]\) \((p \neq \ell)\).
One conjectures, however, that if \(A\) is noetherian and \(\ell\) is invertible in \(A\), one will have
(3.1) \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A) = \dim A \qquad (\ell \text{ invertible in } A) , \]
at least in the most important cases, for example if \(A\) is an excellent ring (EGA IV 7.8.2).

Note that if \(\dim A = 1\), (3.1) is true by 2.3. Moreover, one has the inequality \(\geqslant\) by 2.5 in any case. We will prove later (XIX) that (3.1) is also true if \(A\) is excellent of residue characteristic zero, using resolution of singularities [3]. Here we will prove (3.1) only in the easy case 3.2 below.

Naturally, one has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A) \leqslant 1\) if \(A\) is of characteristic \(\ell\), so this case is trivial. It moreover remains to analyze the case of unequal characteristics, with residue characteristic \(\ell\), and one does not expect 3.1 to be true in that case. One will certainly have to take into account the rank of the module \(\Omega^1_k\) (\(k\) the residue field), i.e. the degree \([k:k^\ell]\).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 3.2

Let \(X\) be a prescheme of finite type over the spectrum of a field \(k\) or over the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring \(R\), and let \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\) be invertible in \(k\) (resp. \(R\)). Then 3.1 is true for every ring \(A\) which is a strict localization of \(X\).
Proof. Take \(X\) integral (one reduces to this case as usual), and let \(n = \dim X\).

Suppose that \(X\) is defined over a separably closed field \(k\). Then for every ring \(A\) which is a strict localization of \(X\) at a closed point, one has \(\dim A = n\). Since each residue field \(K\) of \(R(A)\) is identified with an algebraic extension of \(R(X)\), and since \[ \operatorname{deg.tr.}(R(X)/k) = \dim X = n , \] one has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell K \leqslant n\) by 2.1, whence \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A) \leqslant n\). The opposite inequality is a consequence of 2.5.

Suppose now that \(X\) is of finite type over \(\operatorname{Spec} R\), \(R\) a discrete valuation ring, and let \(A\) be the strict localization of \(X\) at a point \(x\). If \(x\) does not lie over the closed point of \(\operatorname{Spec} R\), one reduces immediately to the case where \(X\) is of finite type over a field (by localizing \(R\)). One can also, for the same reason, assume that the morphism \(X \longrightarrow \operatorname{Spec} R\) is dominant.

Suppose for the moment that moreover \(R\) is a strictly local discrete valuation ring and that the point \(x\) is closed in \(X\). Then one has \(\dim A = \dim X = n\) (EGA IV 5.6.5). Since each residue field \(K\) of \(R(A)\) is identified with a separable extension of \(R(X)\), one has \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A) \leqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(X) &\leqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell L + \operatorname{deg.tr.}(R(X)/L) \\ &= 1 + (n-1) = n \end{aligned} \] by 2.1 and 2.2, where \(L\) is the field of fractions of \(R\), whence the result in this case, taking 2.5 into account.
One deduces the general case from these special cases by means of the following lemma:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 3.3

(i) Let \(X\) be of finite type over the spectrum of a field \(k\), and let \(A\) be a strict localization of \(X\) at a point \(x\). Then there exist a separably closed field \(k'\), a scheme \(X'\) of finite type over \(\operatorname{Spec} k'\), and a point \(x'\) closed in \(X'\), such that \(A\) is isomorphic to a strict localization of \(X'\) at \(x'\).

(ii) Let \(X\) be of finite type over \(\operatorname{Spec} R\), \(R\) a discrete valuation ring, let \(x\) be a point of \(X\) lying over the closed point of \(\operatorname{Spec} R\), and let \(A\) be a strict localization of \(X\) at \(x\). There exist a strictly local discrete valuation ring \(R'\), a scheme \(X'\) of finite type over \(\operatorname{Spec} R'\), and a closed point \(x'\) of \(X'\) lying over the closed point of \(\operatorname{Spec} R'\), such that \(A\) is isomorphic to a strict localization of \(X'\) at \(x'\).

Proof. (i) One can take \(X\) affine. Let \(Y\) be the closure of \(x\) in \(X\), with the reduced induced structure, and let \(d = \dim Y\). By the normalization lemma ([2] Chap. V § 3 n° 1), there exists a morphism \[ X \longrightarrow \operatorname{Spec} k[y_1,\dots ,y_d] = T \] inducing a finite morphism \(Y \longrightarrow T\). Consequently, the strict localization of \(\mathcal{O}_{X,x}\) is isomorphic to the strict localization of \(\mathcal{O}_{X',x'}\), where \(X' = X \times_T \operatorname{Spec} \overline{R}(T)\), and where \(x'\) is a closed point in \(X'\).

(ii) This case is treated in an analogous way. One can assume \(X\) affine, with ring \(A\). Let \(Y\) be the closure of \(x\) in \(X\) with the reduced induced structure, which is a closed subscheme of the closed fibre \(X_0\) of \(X\) over \(\operatorname{Spec} R\), and let \(d = \dim Y\). Then, by lifting the elements \(y_1,\dots,y_d\) of \(A \otimes_R k\) considered in i) to elements of \(A\), one finds a morphism \[ X \longrightarrow \operatorname{Spec} R[y_1,\dots,y_d] = T \] inducing a finite morphism \(Y \longrightarrow T_0\). Let \(R'\) be the strict localization of \(R[y_1,\dots,y_d] = B\) at the prime ideal \(\underline{\mathfrak{m}}B\). Then \(R'\) is a strictly local discrete valuation ring, and one can take \(X' = X \times_T \operatorname{Spec} R'\), and \(x'\) a closed point of \(X'\) lying over \(x\).

pages.title: 4. Cohomological dimension: the case \(\ell\) invertible in \(\mathcal{O}_X\)

blocks.html: 4. Cohomological dimension: the case \(\ell\) invertible in \(\mathcal{O}_X\)

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 4.1

Let \(X\) be a noetherian scheme, \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\), and \(\varphi\) a function on \(X\), with values in \(\mathbb{N}\), satisfying the following conditions:

(i) For each \(x \in X\), \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k(x) \leqslant \varphi(x)\).

(ii) Let \(x \in X\) and \(y \in Y = \) closure of \(x\), \(y \neq x\). Let \(K\) be the ring of rational functions of a strict localization of \(Y\) over \(y\). One has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell K < \varphi(x) - \varphi(y)\).

Then for each \(\ell\)-torsion sheaf \(F\) on \(X\) one has \[ H^q(X,F) = 0 \] if \[ q > \varphi(F) \underset{\text{def}}{=} \operatorname{Sup} \{ \varphi(x) \mid x \in X,\ F_{\bar{x}} \neq 0 \} . \]

Proof. The hypotheses will also be satisfied for the restriction of the function \(\varphi\) to an arbitrary subprescheme of \(X\), so by noetherian induction we can assume the theorem true for each closed subprescheme of \(X\) distinct from \(X\). Let \(F\) be given and write \(F = \varinjlim F_i\) where the \(F_i\) are the constructible subsheaves of \(F\) (IX 2.9 (iii)).

For each \(F_i\), the set of \(x \in X\) such that \(F_x \neq 0\) is constructible in \(X\), and we can apply the induction hypothesis to each \(F_i\) whose support is not dense. One thus sees that the induction hypothesis in fact implies that the theorem is true for each \(F\) which is zero at at least one of the maximal points of \(X\). We will therefore assume that \(F\) does not satisfy this condition.

Now let \(i : \operatorname{Spec} R(X) \longrightarrow X\) be the inclusion, where \(R(X)\) is the ring of rational functions of \(X\), and consider the following exact sequence, where \(K\) and \(C\) are defined as kernel and cokernel respectively: \[ 0 \longrightarrow K \longrightarrow F \longrightarrow i_* i^* F \longrightarrow C \longrightarrow 0 . \]

Here \(K\) and \(C\) are zero at each maximal point of \(X\), so by (ii), \(\varphi(K)\) (resp. \(\varphi(C)\)) is strictly less than \(n = \varphi(F)\), whence \(H^q(X,K) = H^q(X,C) = 0\) for \(q \geqslant n\). Hence to prove \(H^q(X,F) = 0\) for \(q > n\), it suffices, thanks to the exact cohomology sequences, to prove \(H^q(X,i_* i^* F) = 0\), so we can assume that \(F\) is of the form \(i_* G\), for a suitable \(\ell\)-sheaf \(G\) on \(\operatorname{Spec} R(X)\).
Let us examine the Leray spectral sequence. \[ E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X, R^q i_* G) \Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Spec} R(X), G) . \]

Now \(R(X)_{\text{red}}\) is the product of the fields \(k(x)\) for \(x\) maximal in \(X\), so \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell R(X) \leqslant n\) by (i), so the abutment of the spectral sequence is zero in \(\dim > n\).

We want to prove that \(E_2^{p0} = 0\) for \(p > n\). By examining the spectral sequence, one sees that it suffices to prove that \(E_2^{pq} = 0\) if \(q > 0\) and if \(p > n-q-1\). So, by induction, it suffices to prove that \(\varphi(R^q i_* G) < n - q\) for \(q > 0\). But by VIII 5.2 the stalk of \(R^q i_* G\) at a geometric point \(\bar{y}\) over a point \(y \in X\) is none other than \(H^q(\operatorname{Spec} K, G_K)\), where \(K\) is the ring of rational functions of the strict localization of \(X\) at \(\bar{y}\), and \(G_K\) is the induced sheaf on \(\operatorname{Spec} K\). One has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell K < n - \varphi(y)\) by (ii), whence \((R^q i_* G)_{\bar{y}} = 0\) if \(q \geqslant n - \varphi(y)\), which gives the desired result.

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 4.2

Let \(X\) be a noetherian scheme, \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\), \(n \in \mathbb{N}\), and suppose that the following conditions are satisfied:

(i) For each point \(y\) of \(X\) of codimension \(c\), one has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k(y) \leqslant n - 2c\).

(ii) For each ring \(A\), a strict localization of an irreducible closed subscheme \(Y\) of \(X\), one has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A) \leqslant \dim A\).

Then \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell X \leqslant n . \]

More precisely, if \(F\) is an \(\ell\)-sheaf which is zero at each point \(y\) of codimension \(< s\), one has \[ H^q(X,F) = 0 \quad \text{if} \quad q > n - 2s . \]

Indeed, one can take \(\varphi(y) = n-2\operatorname{codim} y\) and apply 4.1, whose condition (i) (resp. (ii)) follows from the corresponding condition (i) (resp. (ii)) of (4.2), taking into account, for (ii), the inequality \(\dim \mathcal{O}_{Y,y} + \dim \mathcal{O}_{X,x} \leqslant \dim \mathcal{O}_{X,y}\).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 4.3

Let \(X\) be of finite type and of dimension \(n\) over a field \(k\), and let \(\ell \neq \operatorname{car} k\). Then \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell X \leqslant 2n + \operatorname{cd}_\ell k\).

One applies the preceding corollary, replacing \(n\) in it by \(2n + \operatorname{cd}_\ell k\), and using 2.1 and 3.2 to verify conditions (i) and (ii) of 4.2, and taking into account, for (i), the inequality \[ \operatorname{deg.tr.} k(y)/k + \dim \mathcal{O}_{X,y} \leqslant \dim X . \]

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 4.4

Let \(X\) be noetherian, and \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\) invertible on \(X\). Suppose that condition (ii) of 4.2 is satisfied, and that moreover \(\ell \neq 2\) or that no residue field of \(X\) is orderable. Then one has \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell X \leqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(X) + \dim X \leqslant 2\operatorname{cd}_\ell R(X) . \]

One sets \(n = \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(X) + \dim X\) in 4.2, and applies 2.4, which implies condition (i) of 4.2, since \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell k(y) \leqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(\mathcal{O}_{X,y}) - \dim \mathcal{O}_{X,y} \leqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(X) - \dim \mathcal{O}_{X,y} \leqslant n - 2 \dim \mathcal{O}_{X,y} . \] The second inequality in 4.4 follows from 2.5.

blocks.title: Example
blocks.html:
Example 4.5

The inelegant hypothesis on residue fields made in 4.4 is necessary, as one sees with \(X = \operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{R}[x,y,z]/(x^2+ y^2+ z^2)\), where all the other conditions are satisfied, with \(\dim X = \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(X) = \ell = 2\), but the sheaf \(\mathbb{Z}/2\) concentrated at the point \((0,0,0)\) has non-zero cohomology in every dimension, so \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell X = + \infty\).

One is also tempted to try, in 4.2, to put hypotheses only on the closed points of \(X\), but this is not possible. For example, there exist discrete valuation rings with algebraically closed residue field and with function field having arbitrarily large cohomological dimension(∗). The spectrum of such a ring will also have very large cohomological dimension.

footnotes.html: (∗) To convince oneself of this, it suffices to note that if \(X\) is a smooth algebraic scheme over a field \(k\), admitting a point \(x \in X(k)\), then one can find a "formal arc of a curve" passing through \(x\) whose "algebraic envelope" is \(X\), and whose function field therefore contains that of \(X\), namely \(K\), and \(y\) induces a discrete valuation whose residue field is \(k\).

blocks.html: 5. Cohomological dimension: the case \(\ell = p\)

Using Artin-Schreier theory (IX 3.5), one obtains a better bound than 4.3 for the \(p\)-cohomological dimension of a scheme \(X\) of characteristic \(p\). Let \(\operatorname{cdqc} X\) be the largest number \(n\) such that \(H^n(X,F) \neq 0\) for at least one quasi-coherent sheaf of Modules \(F\) on \(X\) (in the sense of Zariski). We have the

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 5.1

Let \(X\) be a noetherian scheme of characteristic \(p > 0\). Then \[ \operatorname{cd}_p X \leqslant \operatorname{cdqc} X + 1 . \] In particular, the \(p\)-cohomological dimension of an affine noetherian scheme \(X\) of characteristic \(p > 0\) is at most equal to 1.

Proof. Let us apply IX 5.5: Taking into account the fact that the \(R^q f_* F\), \(q > 0\), are zero for a finite morphism \(f\) and for an abelian sheaf \(F\) (VIII 5.5) (resp. a quasi-coherent sheaf \(F\)), one reduces to proving that \(H^q(X,i_!(\mathbb{Z}/p)_U) = 0\) for \(i : U \longrightarrow X\) an open immersion and for \(q > \operatorname{cdqc} X\).

Now let \(Y\) be a closed subprescheme of \(X\) with support \(X - U\), and let \(J\) be the coherent sheaf of ideals defining \(Y\). The morphism \(\wp : f \longmapsto f^p - f\) (IX 3.5) induces a morphism \(J \longrightarrow J\). By examining the exact sequence IX 3.5 and the exact sequence \[ 0 \longrightarrow i_!(\mathbb{Z}/p)_U \longrightarrow (\mathbb{Z}/p)_X \longrightarrow (\mathbb{Z}/p)_Y \longrightarrow 0 , \] one sees that one in fact has an exact sequence \[ (*) \qquad 0 \longrightarrow i_!(\mathbb{Z}/p)_U \longrightarrow J \longrightarrow J \longrightarrow 0 . \]
Since \(J\) is coherent, one has \(H^q(X,J) = 0\) for \(q > \operatorname{cdqc} X\), whence the result by the exact cohomology sequence.
For a quasi-projective scheme over a separably closed field \(k\), one can reduce this bound in certain cases by 1. In fact, we have the following

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 5.2

Let \(X\) be a scheme of finite type over a field \(k\) of characteristic \(p > 0\). One has \[ \operatorname{cd}_p X \leqslant \dim X + 1 , \] and if \(k\) is separably closed and \(X\) quasi-projective(∗), one has \[ \operatorname{cd}_p X \leqslant \dim X . \]

Indeed, the first assertion is clear, since \(\operatorname{cdqc} X \leqslant \dim X\) ([6] 4.15.2). Let us treat the second: For such an \(X\), the cohomology groups \(H^n(X,F)\) (\(n = \dim X\)), for a coherent sheaf \(F\), are finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(k\). Let \(V = H^n(X,J)\), where \(J\) is the sheaf of ideals appearing in the exact sequence (∗). The morphism \(\varphi : V \longrightarrow V\) deduced from (∗) is obviously of the form \(\varphi = \varepsilon - \operatorname{id}\) where \(\varepsilon\) satisfies \(\varepsilon(rv) = r^p \varepsilon(v)\) for \(r \in k\) and \(v \in V\). The Jacobian of the map \(\Phi\) of the affine scheme deduced from \(\varphi\) is therefore \(-I\), \(I\) the identity matrix. Consequently \(\Phi\) is étale, hence surjective because additive, and it follows that \(\Phi\) is surjective since \(k\) is separably closed, whence the conclusion immediately.

footnotes.html: (∗) Using Chow's lemma, it is easy to replace the condition "\(X\) quasi-projective" by "\(X\) separated".

pages.title: 6. Cohomological dimension for a prescheme of finite type over Spec \(\mathbb{Z}\)

blocks.html: 6. Cohomological dimension for a prescheme of finite type over Spec \(\mathbb{Z}\)

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.1

Let \(X\) be quasi-finite over \(\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}\). Suppose that \(\ell \neq 2\) or that each residue field of \(X\) of characteristic zero is totally imaginary. Then \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell X \leqslant 3\).
This is a consequence of Theorem 2.2 (ii), of Corollary 4.2, and of the fact that a number field (totally imaginary if \(\ell = 2\)) has \(\ell\)-cohomological dimension \(\leqslant 2\) (CG II 4.4).
It in fact follows from class field theory that one has equality if the morphism \(X \longrightarrow \operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}\) is proper and surjective.

Unfortunately, the results of n° 4 do not apply as such if \(X\) is only of finite type over \(\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}\), because hypothesis (ii) of (4.2) is not in general satisfied for the local rings of residue characteristic \(\ell\). One must therefore use the result (5.1) to obtain the correct bound; we are now going to cash in on the theorem (5.1).

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 6.2

Let \(X\) be of finite type over \(\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}\), and let \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\). Suppose, if \(\ell = 2\), that no residue field of \(X\) is orderable. Then \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell X \leqslant 2 \dim X + 1 . \] More precisely, let \(F\) be an \(\ell\)-torsion sheaf such that for every point \(x\) of \(X\) with \(F_{\bar{x}} \neq 0\), one has \[ \dim \{\bar{x}\} \leqslant \begin{cases} (N-1)/2 & \text{if } \ell \neq \operatorname{car} k(x) \\ N-1 & \text{if } \ell = \operatorname{car} k(x) \end{cases} \] (\(\{\bar{x}\}\) is the closure of \(\{x\}\)); then \[ H^p(X,F) = 0 \quad \text{if} \quad p > N . \]

Proof. By induction on \(X\), we can assume the theorem true for each closed subprescheme distinct from \(X\). If \(F\) is as in the statement and if one writes \(F = \varinjlim F_i\) where the \(F_i\) are the constructible subsheaves of \(F\) (IX 2.9 (iii)), each \(F_i\) also satisfies the same hypotheses. It thus suffices to prove the theorem when \(F\) is constructible.

Now in this case the set \(E\) of \(x \in X\) such that \(F_{\bar{x}} \neq 0\) is a constructible subset, and the induction hypothesis implies that the theorem is true for each \(F\) such that \(E\) is not dense. Moreover, the theorem is a consequence of 5.1 for a sheaf concentrated on the fibre at the point \((\ell)\) of \(\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}\), and of 4.3 for a sheaf concentrated on the fibre at \((p)\), where \(p \neq \ell\), taking into account that \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} = 1\) (CG II 2.2).

Take \(X\) reduced, and let \(X = X_0 \cup X_1\) where \(X_1\) is the closed subset, the union of the irreducible components of \(X\) of characteristic \(\ell\), and where \(X_0\) is the union of the other irreducible components, \(X_0\) and \(X_1\) being endowed with the reduced induced structures. Let \(j_\nu : X_\nu \to X\) be the inclusions and let \(d_\nu = \dim X_\nu\), and \(N = \sup\{2d_0+1, d_1+1\}\). For every constructible \(F\) on \(X\), one has an exact sequence \[ (*) \qquad 0 \longrightarrow F \longrightarrow j_{0*} j_0^* F \oplus j_{1*} j_1^* F \longrightarrow C \longrightarrow 0 , \] where \(C\) is concentrated on \(X_0 \cap X_1\), which is of characteristic \(\ell\) and of dimension \(\leqslant d_1-1\). It follows that \[ H^q(X,C) = 0 \quad \text{if} \quad q > N - 1 , \] since by virtue of 5.1 one has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell(X_0 \cap X_1) \leqslant \dim X_0 \cap X_1 + 1 \leqslant d_1 \leqslant N-1\). By examining the relative cohomology exact sequence of (∗), one reduces to the case \(X = X_0\) or \(X = X_1\), and the latter is a consequence of 5.1, as we have already noted.

Suppose then that each maximal point of \(X\) is of characteristic different from \(\ell\), and let \(i_\nu : x_\nu \longrightarrow X\) be the inclusions of the maximal points. By examining the exact sequence \[ 0 \longrightarrow K \longrightarrow F \longrightarrow \bigoplus_\nu i_{\nu*} i_\nu^* F \longrightarrow C \longrightarrow 0 \] one reduces by induction to the case \(F = i_{\nu*} i_\nu^* F\), that is, \(F\) of the form \(i_* G\) for a suitable sheaf \(G\) on \(\operatorname{Spec} k(x)\), \(x\) a point of \(X\). One can therefore assume \(X\) irreducible and reduced, with generic point \(x\), and that the characteristic of \(k(x)\) is zero by 4.3.
Let us examine the spectral sequence \[ (**) \qquad H^p(X, R^q i_* G) \Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Spec} k(x), G) . \]
Let \(s = \dim X\). We must prove that \[ (+) \qquad E_2^{p0} = 0 \quad \text{for } p > 2s + 1 . \]

Now \(k(x)[i]\) is of transcendence degree \(s-1\) over \(\mathbb{Q}[i]\), which is a field of cohomological dimension 2. Since \(k(x)\) is not orderable if \(\ell = 2\), it follows from 2.1 that one has \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell k(x) = s + 1\). This implies that the abutment of the spectral sequence is zero for \(n > s + 1\). It thus suffices, for (+), to prove that in (∗∗) one has \[ (++) \qquad E_2^{pq} = 0 \quad \text{if } p > 2s - q \quad \text{and } q > 0 . \]

Let \(y\) be a point of \(X\) and \(K\) the ring of fractions of a strict localization at a geometric point \(\tilde{y}\) of \(X\) over \(y\). Then \(K\) is a direct product of fields each of which is of degree of transcendence \(s-1\) over a strict localization of \(\mathbb{Z}\), and one thus has, by 2.1 and 2.2, \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell K \leqslant s\). Moreover, one can apply 3.2 if the residue characteristic of \(y\) is not \(\ell\). One thus has

(") \[ (R^q i_* G)_{\tilde{y}} = 0 \begin{cases} \text{if } q > \operatorname{codim} y, \text{ i.e. } \dim \bar{y} > s-q, \text{ and } \ell \neq \operatorname{car} k(y), \\ \text{or if } q > s \text{ in any case.} \end{cases} \]
In particular we have \(E_2^{pq} = 0\) if \(q > s\). To verify (++) in the case \(0 < q \leqslant s\), we apply the induction hypothesis to the sheaves \(R^q i_*(G)\).

By the statement and ("), we must set \(N' = 2s - q\) and verify the two inequalities \[ s - q \leqslant (N'-1)/2 \] \[ s-1 = \dim X_\ell \leqslant N'-1 , \] where \(X_\ell\) is the fibre of \(X\) over the point \((\ell)\) of \(\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}\). They are indeed true if \(0 < q \leqslant s\), q.e.d.
